title: What churches and Christian publishers have said about AI, 2019 to 2026
subtitle: Statements, resolutions, policies and surveys, with Catholic documents marked
caption: Evangelical bodies spoke first, in 2019. Most of the rest has come since 2025, as AI moved from the seminar to the church office.

cells: The Ethics & Religious Liberty Commission of the Southern Baptist Convention releases "Artificial Intelligence: An Evangelical Statement of Principles," a preamble and 12 articles signed by evangelical leaders.
June 2023
Southern Baptist messengers adopt "On Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technologies," calling for "eschatological hope rather than uncritical embrace or fearful rejection."
The Vatican issues Antiqua et Nova (Catholic): AI "should not be seen as an artificial form of human intelligence but as a product of it."
NAE president Walter Kim and BioLogos president Kristine Torjesen sign a Christian and Jewish joint statement on AI ethics at a summit in Rome.
Gloo, a church technology company, releases a benchmark testing how leading AI models answer questions of Christian faith and values.
Christianity Today publishes its AI policy for writers: "We do not write with AI."
Lifeway Research releases its surveys of Protestant pastors and churchgoers on AI.
Pope Leo XIV signs Magnifica Humanitas, his first encyclical, on the human person in the time of AI; it is presented May 25 (Catholic).
June 2026
Lifeway releases the Brentwood Statement on AI and Christian Ministry: "Disciple making is a uniquely human practice that cannot be automated or outsourced in the name of efficiency and convenience."
The Gospel Coalition tells writers not to use AI for ideating, research beyond a basic fact search, organizing, writing, or editing beyond a basic spelling check.
The Presbyterian Church in America names the members of its ad interim study committee on artificial intelligence, due to report no later than the 2028 General Assembly.
The NAE board adopts a resolution on AI: it "does not bear the image of God; it possesses no conscience, no love, no soul."
